name: Song dynasty
summary: Period with major developments in painting, calligraphy, urban life and ceramics; literati and court pictorial traditions should not be conflated.

wardrobe.text: restrained layered robes; exact silhouette and headwear depend on gender/status/subperiod

textiles_materials.text: high-fired stoneware/porcelain traditions including celadon and monochrome wares

hairstyle_headwear.text: official/scholar headwear and women’s hair should be selected from dated works rather than Tang/Ming defaults

architecture.text: timber halls, gardens, urban river/canal contexts depending on region

interior_furniture.text: tables, chairs, screens and scholar furnishings in elite contexts

food_drink_tableware.text: refined ceramic tea and dining vessels

writing_calligraphy.text: calligraphy as a core elite art; use real or intentionally omitted text

lighting_technology.text: lamps/candles in interiors; daylight dominant in painting-derived transformations

incompatible_or_anachronistic.text: Tang high-waisted court styling copied wholesale
blue-and-white porcelain as a generic Song signature

prompt_fragments.ink: For a Song-oriented ink transformation, let brush line, ink density, blank paper/silk and spatial rhythm carry the image; do not simulate a photograph with an ink filter.

scope_note: Foundation pack: use as a bounded starting point, not an encyclopedia.
strict_reconstruction_note: Strict mode must choose Northern/Southern Song, region, role, and pictorial/object evidence family.
